title: Transnistria
summary: Transnistria, officially referred to as the Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic (PMR), is a landlocked breakaway entity recognized internationally as part of Moldova. It is situated along the Dniester River and borders Ukraine, with significant implications for regional stability and ethnic relations.

sections.heading: Geographical Context
paragraphs: Transnistria is located between the [[dniester|Dniester]] River and the Moldova–[[ukraine|Ukraine]] border, controlling a narrow strip of land. The capital and largest city of Transnistria is Tiraspol. The region is recognized by Moldova as the [[administrative-territorial-entity-of-ukraine|Administrative-Territorial]] Units of the Left Bank of the Dniester.

sections.heading: Historical Background
paragraphs: The origins of Transnistria can be traced back to the Moldavian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic (MASSR), established in 1924 within the [[ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic|Ukrainian SSR]]. The area underwent significant changes during World War II, leading to the creation of the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic in 1940. In 1990, amidst [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]]'s dissolution, the Pridnestrovian Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic was declared, aiming to remain within the Soviet Union amid fears of Moldova's potential unification with Romania.

sections.heading: Conflict and Ceasefire
paragraphs: A military conflict erupted between Transnistria and Moldova in March 1992, concluding with a ceasefire in July of the same year. This ceasefire led to the establishment of a Joint Control Commission involving Moldova, Russia, and Transnistria, along with a trilateral peacekeeping force.

sections.heading: Political Status and Citizenship
paragraphs: Transnistria operates as a de facto independent semi-presidential republic, possessing its own government, military, and currency. Despite its unrecognized status, most residents hold Moldovan citizenship, with many also having Russian, Romanian, or [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] citizenship. The population is primarily composed of Russians, Moldovans (Romanians), and [[ukrainians|Ukrainians]].

sections.heading: International Relations and Recognition
paragraphs: Transnistria is categorized as a post-Soviet 'frozen conflict' zone, alongside [[republic-of-abkhazia|Abkhazia]] and South Ossetia, and maintains friendly relations with these regions. In March 2022, the [[parliamentary-assembly-of-the-council-of-europe|Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe]] passed a resolution designating the territory as under military occupation by Russia.
